newsitem.title: CHILE: El Teniente unions to vote Tuesday on wage offers.
newsitem.headline: El Teniente unions to vote Tuesday on wage offers.

text.p: Workers at Codelco's 340,000-tonne-a- year El Teniente copper mine will vote Tuesday on whether to accept either of two wage packages reached in talks with unions this week, a Codelco official said Friday.

Management and union officials met for talks on Wednesday and Thursday to hammer out details of the wage offers, said the official by telephone from the mine near Rancagua, about 100 km south of Santiago.
Unions will officially inform workers of the details of the offers at assemblies on Monday and then vote late on Tuesday, said the official.
"We believe one of the packages will be accepted and that we'll have a settlement next week," said the official.
Union leaders could not be reached for comment.
The contract at El Teniente, Chile's third largest copper mine, won't expire until the end of the year. Neither union nor management officials have seen any immediate possibility of a strike.

Both offers grant a 3.2 percent real wage increase annually. But one package calls for a 42-month contract, a bonus of 800,000 pesos ($1,918) upon signing and a 400,000 peso ($960) low-interest loan to workers who want it, while the other offer has a 48-month contract, a one million pesos ($2,400) bonus and a 700,000 peso ($1,680) low-interest loan.
Unions had insisted going into talks on a maximum 36-month contract.

Labor relations at El Teniente, Codelco's only mainly underground mine, have usually been better than at other Codelco pits, particularly Chuquicamata, but statements this week by union leaders suggested tension in the wage talks. Still, union leaders said they saw no danger of strikes before the contract ends on December 31.
